rules.title: No premature optimisation
rules.what: Do not optimise what is not proven hot. Profile first, optimise the measured hot path, and keep the profile as evidence.
rules.why: Optimised cold code costs readability for no gain; the guess about what is hot is usually wrong by a wide margin.
rules.how: Run the workload with a profiler, rank by total time, optimise the top items, re-measure, keep both profiles.

verify.how: Before/after profiles on the same workload accompany the optimisation commit.

rules.title: Complexity under control on growing inputs
rules.what: Code paths that receive growing inputs avoid quadratic-or-worse behaviour (nested loops, repeated contains on linear structures); data structures match the access pattern.
rules.why: O(n^2) on user data is the pattern that makes a service die on the day it succeeds: it works perfectly until the data grows, then it melts.
rules.how: For collection processing: hash-map lookups instead of nested scans, early exits, single-pass aggregation; state the input-size assumption in a comment when it matters.

patterns.note: Linear membership scan inside loops; candidate for Set/Map.

verify.how: Complexity test: runtime on 2x input stays within the stated growth budget (not 4x).

limits: Nested loops over two small bounded collections are fine; the audit finding is a candidate, not a verdict.

rules.title: Stream and chunk large data
rules.what: Process data larger than memory in a stream or by chunks; never load a whole large file, result set or payload into memory at once.
rules.why: Loading whole datasets caps the service at the size of its largest file and pays the full memory cost for data mostly passed over.
rules.how: Iterators/generators, chunked reads, HTTP streaming, cursor queries; cap and reject payloads above the stated maximum.

patterns.note: Whole-file read; candidate if the file is user-supplied or unbounded.

verify.how: Processing a file larger than the memory budget completes within bounded memory.

limits: Small config files read whole are fine; the rule targets data that grows.

rules.title: Beware catastrophic regex
rules.what: Regular expressions applied to untrusted input avoid unbounded backtracking: no nested quantifiers on ambiguous patterns; prefer a parser for structured input.
rules.why: A catastrophic-backtracking regex turns one hostile input into a service outage: exponential CPU on a single thread, blocking everything behind it.
rules.how: Test the regex with adversarial inputs; avoid (.*)+ patterns; bound input length; use a real parser for structured formats (URLs, dates, JSON).

patterns.note: Nested quantified groups; classic backtracking risk; verify with adversarial input.

verify.how: Adversarial-input test completes within the time budget or rejects cleanly.

rules.title: Memoise or precompute repeated work
rules.what: Work repeated with the same inputs is computed once: memoise pure functions, precompute on write when many reads pay for it, or cache (NR-BACK-003).
rules.why: Recomputation is the quiet cost multiplier: it wastes the same CPU on every request when one computation with a stored result would serve.
rules.how: Identify pure repeated computations, memoise with a bounded store, or move the computation to write-time when the read/write ratio justifies it.

verify.how: Compute count per unit of work decreased; measured on the workload.

limits: Memoisation of impure or volatile functions creates bugs; purity first, speed second.

rules.title: Bound concurrent work
rules.what: Concurrency (threads, coroutines, workers) is bounded to the platform's real capacity; unbounded fan-out is replaced by queues with limits.
rules.why: Concurrency beyond capacity multiplies context switching, memory and failure rate while throughput goes down - the extra workers do damage, not work.
rules.how: Pool sizes from measured throughput curves, queue with backpressure upstream, cap parallel requests per client.

patterns.note: Unbounded Promise.all over a mapped collection; candidate for a concurrency-limited runner.
Pool with default size; verify it matches the machine profile.

verify.how: Load beyond the bound: queueing or rejection, no worker explosion; throughput curve stays on its plateau.

rules.title: Fail fast, avoid zombie work
rules.what: Invalid input is rejected at the entry point; long work checks a cancellation signal; failures stop dependent work instead of continuing to completion.
rules.why: Work done on invalid or already-failed premises consumes the full cost for a result that will be discarded: the most expensive computation is the one nobody needed.
rules.how: Validate at the boundary, propagate cancellation (abort signals, ctx.Err, interruption flags), short-circuit dependent steps on failure.

verify.how: Cancellation mid-work stops dependent calls; invalid input rejected before any expensive processing.

rules.title: Use the platform's async/blocking model correctly
rules.what: Blocking work never occupies a platform's event loop: async runtimes get awaited I/O, thread-based runtimes get pooled blocking calls; CPU-bound work goes off the request path.
rules.why: One blocked event loop stalls every concurrent request behind it; blocking work is a scalability bug disguised as a slow function.
rules.how: In Node: no sync filesystem/crypto in handlers, CPU-heavy work to worker threads or queues. In async Python: no blocking calls without offloading. State the model in the service design.

patterns.note: Sync call in a JS codebase; verify it is not on the request path.
Blocking sleep; in async code use asyncio.sleep and verify the context.

verify.how: Concurrency test: one slow operation does not delay unrelated concurrent requests beyond budget.

limits: Startup-only or CLI code may block; the rule targets the request path.

rules.title: Memory bounded, swap avoided
rules.what: Runtime memory has an explicit budget; hot paths avoid unbounded retention (growing caches, leaked references, whole-dataset copies); swapping is treated as a defect.
rules.why: Swapping turns compute into disk I/O on a path meant to be fast: latency multiplies, and the hardware's useful work collapses. Growing memory is the same failure in slow motion.
rules.how: Cap caches and buffers, profile allocations on the hot path, watch swap counters, alert on growth trends.

patterns.note: Full-copy of a possibly large structure; candidate inside loops.

verify.how: Memory profile flat under sustained load; no swap on the production workload.
